mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Mondeo Vignale engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Ford Mondeo Vignale engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,000 for supply only, while used units start from around £600.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of Ford Mondeo Vignale engine failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Owners of the Ford Mondeo Vignale should watch for persistent limp mode, excessive black smoke from the exhaust (diesel), or a noticeable loss of power under acceleration.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Mondeo Vignale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Given that Mk4 and Mk5 Ford Mondeo Vignale models typically hold a market value between £6,000 and £15,000, a full rebuilt engine is often a financially viable investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Mondeo Vignale engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply-only delivery of a Ford Mondeo Vignale engine takes 1 to 3 working days via nationwide courier.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the QXWA and UNBA engines in the Ford Mondeo Vignale?

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Mondeo Vignale - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched as the ultra-premium flagship trim of the Mondeo range, the Vignale variant debuted in the Mk4 generation and continued into the Mk5, offering luxury appointments alongside Ford's most refined 2.0-litre diesel, petrol, and hybrid powertrains.

milestones.description: QXWA, 2.0L Diesel, 150PS/180PS - Introduced with the Mk4 Mondeo Vignale, featuring refined NVH damping, premium specification, and robust Duratorq torque.
UNBA, 2.0L Petrol, 203PS - High-output EcoBoost option for the Vignale, offering smooth, quiet performance and strong acceleration.
QXWB / U6BA, 2.0L Diesel (190PS) / 2.0L Hybrid (187PS) - Mk5 facelift brought updated EcoBlue diesel efficiency and the introduction of the self-charging hybrid powertrain to the Vignale lineup.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Mondeo Vignale Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Mondeo Vignale is a refined, premium vehicle, but its 2.0-litre powertrains are not immune to wear. The QXWA (diesel) and UNBA (petrol) codes dominate replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR & DPF Clogging - Why the Ford Mondeo Vignale (QXWA/QXWB) Restricts Airflow
problems.rootCause: Urban driving prevents the DPF from completing active regeneration cycles, while exhaust gases recirculated by the EGR valve deposit heavy carbon soot, restricting airflow and triggering limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical DPF clean and EGR maintenance.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage clogging, but does not fix underlying mechanical wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when carbon damage has caused secondary issues like turbo starvation or severe compression loss.

problems.recommendation: For Mondeo Vignale owners, maintaining the premium driving experience is paramount. If the engine block is fundamentally sound, targeted component repair (e.g., EGR service or thermostat replacement) is the most cost-effective route. However, if catastrophic overheating or severe internal wear has occurred, a reconditioned engine is the most reliable long-term solution to preserve the vehicle's refinement and value.

problems.h4: Coolant Leaks & Head Gasket Failure - Why the Ford Mondeo Vignale (UNBA/UNBB) Overheats
problems.rootCause: Plastic thermostat housing degradation or head gasket wear allows coolant to escape, leading to overheating and potential engine damage if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip top end, replace head gasket/thermostat, flush cooling system.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable only if the block is confirmed free of cracks and porosity via pressure testing.

repairOptions.longevity: The right call when overheating has warped the cylinder head or caused internal damage.

items.question: What are the common signs of Ford Mondeo Vignale engine failure?
items.answer: Owners of the Ford Mondeo Vignale should watch for persistent limp mode, excessive black smoke from the exhaust (diesel), or a noticeable loss of power under acceleration.
keyPoints: A "milkshake" appearance on the oil filler cap indicates coolant has mixed with the engine oil.
If the engine management light is flashing alongside these symptoms, stop driving immediately.
Continuing to drive can cause catastrophic internal damage to the turbocharger or engine block.
items.cta: -> Compare repair vs replacement costs for your Ford Mondeo Vignale

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Mondeo Vignale?
items.answer: Given that Mk4 and Mk5 Ford Mondeo Vignale models typically hold a market value between £6,000 and £15,000, a full rebuilt engine is often a financially viable investment.
keyPoints: For older Mk4 models valued under £8,000, sourcing a verified low-mileage used engine may be the most financially sensible option.
A rebuilt unit is highly recommended for newer Mk5 models, as the cost is comfortably absorbed by the vehicle's higher retained value.
Always weigh the replacement cost against the vehicle's current market value before committing.

items.answer: A standard supply-only delivery of a Ford Mondeo Vignale engine takes 1 to 3 working days via nationwide courier.
keyPoints: If you opt for a supply & fit service, the physical installation and testing process typically requires 1 to 2 days at a specialist garage.
Total turnaround time from quote to completion is usually under a week.
This depends entirely on parts availability and your chosen supplier's schedule.

items.question: What is the difference between the QXWA and UNBA engines in the Ford Mondeo Vignale?
items.answer: The QXWA code is a 2.0-litre Duratorq diesel producing 150PS to 190PS, favoured for high-mileage motorway cruising and torque.
keyPoints: The UNBA code is a 2.0-litre EcoBoost petrol producing 203PS, offering smoother, quieter performance and quicker acceleration.
They are not interchangeable and require entirely different ECU calibrations and mounting setups.
Always verify your exact engine code via your V5C logbook or registration before ordering a replacement.
